questions.explain: The chapter requires completeness, timeliness, structure, and self-referential integrity — the monitoring pipeline itself must be monitored so a dead collector doesn't leave the engine flying blind.
options: Completeness, timeliness, structure, and self-referential integrity
Volume, velocity, variety, and veracity
Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score
Collection, storage, visualization, and alerting
questions.q: Which four properties must telemetry satisfy for autonomous operation?

questions.explain: The sidecar-plus-external-aggregator topology keeps the aggregator and decision engine on independent infrastructure; the decision engine never talks directly to the database node for telemetry, so a failed primary is still observable via the replica's sidecar.
options: Run the metrics agent inside the primary's SQL Server process for low latency
Place the Prometheus aggregator on the primary node
Run a lightweight sidecar collector co-located with each node pushing to a remote aggregator on independent infrastructure; the decision engine reads only from the aggregator
Have the decision engine query sys.dm_exec_requests directly on each node
questions.q: How does the chapter recommend making metric pipelines survive the failure of the primary they monitor?

questions.explain: The mssql_unreachable gauge is subscribed by the decision engine via Alertmanager as a trigger for failover evaluation, correlated with replica health to distinguish true failure from a collector-only network partition.
options: To record long-term availability SLAs for monthly reporting
To trigger failover evaluation in the autonomous decision engine after correlating with replica health signals
To page the DBA immediately when a scrape fails
To automatically restart the sql_exporter process
questions.q: What is the autonomous purpose of the mssql_unreachable gauge emitted by the resilient collection agent?

questions.explain: Tier 1 = absolute violations; Tier 2 = baseline deviations (P99 > 2× the 7-day baseline); Tier 3 = trend projections such as predict_linear forecasting the send queue exceeding 10GB in 45 minutes.
options: Absolute violations, baseline deviations, trend projections
Critical, warning, informational
Node-level, cluster-level, application-level
CPU, memory, disk, network
questions.q: What are the three tiers of the chapter's autonomous alerting architecture?

questions.explain: The chapter pairs a columnstore metric-history table (what the system was doing) with SQL Server temporal tables (what the system was configured to do, via FOR SYSTEM_TIME queries) as the two memory dimensions.
options: A Prometheus remote-write archive and a local SQLite cache
A columnstore metric-history table plus SQL Server temporal tables with FOR SYSTEM_TIME history for configuration changes
Two mirrored sql_exporter instances
An Azure Monitor log analytics workspace and a Grafana dashboard
questions.q: Which two memory-layer components does the chapter prescribe, and what does each record?
